title: Parameterize Function

solutions.title: One rise, a lookup table for the tier
solutions.tradeoff: The three tier amounts move from three type-checked function names into one untyped-at-the-call-site number, so a caller that gets the wrong literal now fails at runtime (a wrong test assertion) instead of failing to compile.

reviewFocus: Was `raiseRestrictedViewBand` folded into the merged function, or does it still stand apart? Folding it erases the price cap the venue's letting agreement requires - that is the exercise, not an edge case of it.
Is the merged function's parameter named `amount` or `value` anywhere, even as an intermediate step that got left in? Neither reads at a call site.
Does the parameter name carry the unit, the way `paceSecondsPerKm` does in the naming conventions table - or does it only carry the direction (a rise) and leave the unit implicit?
Did `raiseByFive`, `raiseByTen`, and `raiseByTwenty` disappear entirely, or does one of them survive somewhere as a thin wrapper nobody calls?
Does the walkthrough show a rejected name for the merged function itself, not only for its parameter?
